clue.text: Hat leaving Charlie with rings — bowler sometimes does this

indicators.note: leaving means one letter goes out of the hat word, departing from it

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
peals are rings of bells

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a bowler losing a hat while bells ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler shouts to the umpire for a batter to be given out; that call is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the bowler calls on the umpire for a dismissal, which is termed making a plea of that kind.

clue.text: Animal from mountain area: tailless cat

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the feline word, three letters

explanation.surface: A mountain animal resembling a cat missing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American camelid kept for wool is one kind of animal.

clue.text: Very hot farm animal gripping leg

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so the farm animal wraps round the leg word

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
pin is informal for leg

explanation.surface: A hot pig holding its own leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot is an idiom for food that is extremely hot.

clue.text: Take on board ace pirate at sea around Portugal

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A pirate captain at sea near Portugal, taking things on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ACE PIRATE into APRECIATE; 'around' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on board is an idiom meaning to understand or recognise fully.

clue.text: Fleet Street admitting endless trouble and strife

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the street abbreviation contains the next piece
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang for a man's spouse

explanation.surface: Fleet Street, home of British newspapers, letting in endless trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble and strife' is Cockney rhyming slang for the spouse; Fleet Street is London's old newspaper street.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means fast or quick, a synonym.

clue.text: Pictures can be seen here since getting developed, enthralling mother

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the shuffled letters hold the next piece inside
developed suggests film turned into something new, so the letters of since are rearranged

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Film photos being developed while a mother looks on, enthralled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting developed' turns SINCE into CINES, and 'enthralling' puts MA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Films are informally called the pictures, and picture houses are where they are shown.

clue.text: One might investigate Russian satellite company with dodgy amounts

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or off, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A company with dodgy accounts investigated over a Russian satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet space traveller might be sent to inspect a Russian satellite in orbit.

clue.text: Tidy Welsh town? Almost

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: Neath is a town in south Wales

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Welsh town is tidy, and almost conceding it.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a town in south Wales near Swansea.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and tidy are synonyms for orderly.

clue.text: One working on an estate, say, crazy to collect heads of every Cape hyacinth

definitions.text: One working on an estate, say

indicators.note: to collect means to gather inside, so the crazy word holds the initials

parts.note: manic means wild or crazy

indicators.note: heads of means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A crazed estate worker gathering hyacinths from the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is an estate car, a British station wagon; 'estate' wants to be land.
explanation.definitionFit: A car repairer works on vehicles, an estate car being one example.

clue.text: South American writer regularly sets up tension

parts.note: US means American
a pen is a writer

indicators.note: up in a down clue means reading the letters upwards, backwards
regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A South American author sets up tension in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes E and S from 'sets'; 'up' turns them to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious uncertainty about what will happen next is a synonym for tension.

clue.text: Appear excited to follow dad

indicators.note: to follow places the excited word after the word for dad

parts.note: pop is an American word for father
up can mean worked up or excited

explanation.surface: Someone getting excited to tag along after their father.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view suddenly is the phrasal-verb meaning of the answer, close in sense to show up.

clue.text: Trendy positions for cases

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
stances are positions or postures

explanation.surface: Fashionable stances taken on behalf of legal cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name examples or occurrences of something, as in 'in several cases'.

clue.text: Link prisoner with new wing getting defaced?

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: defaced here means losing its face, the front letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a section, as in a wing or division of a building or organisation

explanation.surface: A prison scene: an inmate in a new wing with vandalised walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie or relationship between two things is a link; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: China tea

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means a friend or pal
a South American herbal infusion drunk like tea

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain and a cup of tea, a two-word tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with the friend word, so China means pal.
explanation.definitionFit: China is rhyming slang for a pal, and the same spelling names a South American infusion, a type of tea.

clue.text: Queen ruined glorious year, strictly

parts.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A queen's glorious year ruined, strictly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a thorough, exacting way is a synonym for strictly.

clue.text: Resemblances I initially missed caught by Israeli — it's strange

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the shuffled letters surround the other piece
strange signals that the letters are put in an odd new order
initially picks the opening letter of missed

explanation.surface: Someone notes they first missed a likeness, which an Israeli then spotted, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges ISRAELI and IT'S into SILARITIES, and 'caught by' puts I plus M inside it after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of likeness between things are synonyms for this plural noun.

clue.text: Playwright quietly leaving female before conflict

indicators.note: leaving means the quiet letter departs from the playwright's name

parts.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A playwright quietly leaves a woman ahead of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash or come into opposition with something is a synonym for conflict as a verb.

clue.text: Artist's model put closer — eyesight's beginning to go

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape or mould, so the letters are reworked
to go means the letter picked from the next word is taken out of the shuffle
beginning picks the first letter of eyesight's

explanation.surface: An artist's model told to move closer because the painter's eyesight is failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' rearranges PUT CLOSER, and 'to go' says the E from eyesight's is not used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carves or models statues is one kind of artist.

clue.text: Those who steal shoes

definitions.meaning: people who steal, that is move stealthily

explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy creepers are people who move quietly; the same word names soft-soled trainers.

clue.text: Walk ignoring a learner's state of physique

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so letters are dropped from the walk word

parts.note: a constitutional is a walk taken for one's health
L is for learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A walking instructor ignores a learner's fitness level.
explanation.walkthrough: A constitutional is a gentle stroll for the health; drop one A and the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's physical make-up or general health is described by this word, as in 'a strong build'.

clue.text: Fruitcake — some Ellen miserably picked up

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, read from bottom to top
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A fruitcake is picked up by Ellen, who is feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes LENMIS from 'Ellen miserably'; 'picked up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich fruit cake with marzipan, traditionally made for Easter, is one kind of fruitcake.

clue.text: Just depend on this setter? On the contrary!

indicators.note: on the contrary says swap the order the clue gave, so the setter goes on top

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
to rely is to depend

explanation.surface: The setter asks if you can depend on them, then cheekily says the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depend on this setter' gives RELY on ME; the contrary puts ME on RELY, above it in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as in 'only' or 'simply' is a synonym for the adverb.

clue.text: Left bumpkin's farmhouse?

parts.note: an oaf is a clumsy, bumpkin-like person; 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin's farmhouse, abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a farmhouse is a style of bread, not a building here.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhouse is a type of rustic bread baked in a tin, one example of a baked bread shape.

clue.text: Stroll over with most of linen — it's suitable for jumpers

parts.note: to tramp is to walk or stroll
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is used

explanation.surface: A stroll with linen garments that suit someone wearing jumpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' suggests woolly sweaters, but it means people who jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung canvas frame is made for bouncing on, so it suits people leaping up and down.

clue.text: Satisfied aluminium is this

parts.note: met as in having met a need, satisfied it
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A statement that aluminium, contentedly, is one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium is an example of an element of this class, so the whole clue defines it.

clue.text: Celebrity scoundrels on the rise

indicators.note: on the rise in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: rats are scoundrels or traitors

explanation.surface: A celebrity's scoundrel associates rising in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous performer is commonly called by this word, a synonym.

clue.text: Present minutes before hospital department's medical attention

parts.note: a treat is a present or gift
ENT is the ear, nose and throat hospital department

explanation.surface: A gift handed over minutes before a hospital department attends to a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Care given to a patient by doctors is a synonym for medical attention.

clue.text: Pick up smell, perhaps

definitions.meaning: smell is one of the five faculties of perception

explanation.surface: Detecting an odour in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive is the verb; smell is one example of the faculties of perception, the noun.

clue.text: What tennis player might do after a fault — hold back

definitions.text: What tennis player might do after a fault
definitions.meaning: after a failed first serve the player delivers the ball again
to keep something aside for later use

explanation.surface: A tennis player takes a second serve, holding back on power.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as RE-SERVE: serve again.
explanation.definitionFit: Read split it means serve again, as after a tennis fault; whole it means keep back or set aside.

clue.text: Allegiance from 50 kings and queens? Not at first

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: kings and queens are royalty

explanation.surface: Fifty monarchs inspiring loyalty, but not from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness to a sovereign or cause is a synonym for allegiance.
